patch.value:
Found while reviewing the pull request that fixes issue 287 (repeat-import no-op). That pull request restored Projects push to main's behaviour to keep its scope, so both defects remain on main.


With one native item and an empty board, build two push plans before either applies. Applying both produces two remote drafts and two board tags on the same item. Separately, let `addProjectV2DraftIssue` return a card ID and reject `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue`. Current `main` reports `Sync wrote nothing; 1 operation(s) failed.` after the provider has accepted the attachment. The previous PR implementation returned `pushed: 1, pushFailed: 0` in JSON for that same partial outcome.

Before attachment, revalidate the live board and complete tracker binding, including tags for cards absent from the original snapshot. Preserve or reconcile the confirmed card ID before retrying. Expose attachment, status, and tracker-tag results in JSON and TOON with an explicit partial outcome. Add real non-git tracker tests proving that two stale plans yield one card and one tag, and that a status refusal remains visible while retry reuses the attached card.
Projects push: fence stale attachment plans and report partial outcomes (duplicate drafts; a rejected status write after an accepted attachment reports nothing written)

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Behavioral revert proofs in a disposable copy: seven isolated changes caused seven expected failures. Running the stale entry created two cards, dropping the absent-card and peer-claim guards lost their refusals, rethrowing the Status failure lost the accepted attachment receipt, discarding the retained card ID prevented recovery, restoring automatic 5xx retries replayed draft creation, and omitting pushReceipts broke the packed formatter check. The broad related run passed 1975 cases and flagged two old fixture expectations. Both corrected cases passed the targeted rerun, giving 1977 passing distinct cases across 68 related files.

value.text: The linked runner supplies an isolated PM_PATH. Two new fault-injection fixtures assumed implicit root discovery ignored it, so their recovery paths pointed at the runner's empty tracker. Their helpers now explicitly resolve the fixture tracker, matching the normal command path. Product code needed no change.
